actions.reason: C0001 has a coherent RNA-defined biological identity with strong, FDR-significant downregulation of metabolic pathways (large effect sizes). WXS and CNV are not significant but do not actively contradict the RNA signal. Measured technical factors do not provide a dominant per-set explanation, and structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. Retaining C0001 for downstream validation is better supported than Drop.

C0002 shows moderate cross-modal support: CNV has multiple FDR-significant continuous losses, WXS shows a strong nominal PBRM1 enrichment, and RNA has several FDR-significant pathways. Patient support is moderate (median 2). Technical factors are not per-set significant. Structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. The candidate is sufficiently defensible for retention.

C0003 lacks a coherent biological identity: only one RNA pathway is FDR-significant, WXS and CNV show no significant findings, and cross-modal consistency is weak (only CT positive, with some patients having zero support). No positive structural evidence supports Split or Merge, and no extra evidence is available to resolve the uncertainty. The candidate is not sufficiently defensible for downstream validation.

C0004 has no significant biological findings in any modality (RNA, WXS, CNV all non-significant after FDR correction). Cross-modal consistency is weak and internal structure is unstable (high PAC). Technical factors are not per-set significant, but the absence of a coherent molecular identity and lack of positive structural support for Split or Merge make Drop better supported than retention.

C0005 is strongly confounded by technical factors: per-set tests show significant associations with CT manufacturer, scanner model, and reconstruction kernel, and the CT modality provides the dominant separation (median silhouette 0.274). Biological evidence is absent (no significant RNA, WXS, or CNV findings). The measured technical explanation plausibly dominates the identity, so Drop is better supported than retention.

C0006 has strong biological support: RNA shows FDR-significant inflammatory/interferon upregulation and myogenesis downregulation with large effect sizes, and WXS shows significant BAP1 enrichment. Cross-modal consistency is moderate (RNA and WSI positive, highest patient support median 3). Technical factors are not per-set significant. Structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. Retaining C0006 for downstream validation is better supported than Drop.
